meta.title: {brand} — Turn your technical documentation into revenue
meta.description: {brand} pays digital companies to use their technical documentation, tickets and code to train and evaluate AI models. Non-exclusive licence, company name removed, fixed payment.

hero.eyebrow: Technical documentation · Licence of use · Training data
hero.title: Your teams have produced years of documentation.| It can still generate revenue.
hero.lead: {brand} pays digital companies to use some of their internal content (technical documentation, tickets, code and code reviews) to train and evaluate AI models.
hero.sub: You keep ownership of your content and your software. Scope, permitted uses and payment are set out in a contract.
facts: Non-exclusive licence: you keep your content
Company name removed from the data

useCases.label: Who it is for
useCases.title: Four situations,| one approach
useCases.intro: Documentation can be given value at several points in the life of a digital company.

items.title: Operating company
items.text: Additional revenue, without giving up any of your business or your content.

items.title: Voluntary wind-down
items.text: Dissolution or solvent liquidation: plan it before online accounts are closed.

items.title: Divestment or product shutdown
items.text: The documentation of a discontinued product can be valued separately.

items.title: Judicial liquidation
items.text: With the liquidator and on authorization of the supervising judge.

scope.title: What the licence covers,| and what it excludes
scope.intro: The exact scope is agreed in writing before anything is signed. Depending on what is agreed, it can include:

buy.title: Included depending on scope
items: Wikis and Notion or Confluence spaces
Tickets: Jira, Linear, GitHub Issues
Specifications, runbooks and postmortems
Repository source code, with its history: commits, pull requests and reviews

notBuy.title: Always excluded
items: Messaging: Slack, Teams, email
Customer files and production databases
HR and legal spaces
Personal data of customers and employees
Code written for clients or under a third-party licence

scope.note: Source code can therefore be part of the scope. The licence does not transfer its ownership: it only permits its use to train and evaluate AI models. It grants no right to run, distribute or commercialize your software. Your brand and domain names are not affected, and you remain free to sell the software.

process.title: How it works
process.intro: The steps depend on the company's situation. Choose your case.

steps.title: First conversation
steps.text: You tell us about your business, the tools you use and the period your archives cover.

steps.title: Inventory under NDA
steps.text: Review of tools, volume and age of the content, under a non-disclosure agreement.

steps.title: Assessment and proposal
steps.text: A written proposal setting out scope, exclusions and amount, or a note that a licence is not relevant.

steps.title: Agreement and payment
steps.text: Signature of the non-exclusive licence of use; the fixed amount is paid at signature.

steps.title: Export and preparation
steps.text: Export of the content, removal of identifying elements, then deletion of the raw exports.

aside.title: What you get
items: Revenue from content you already own
Ownership of your content and your software, unchanged
Scope and exclusions agreed in writing
Export and preparation carried out by us

tabs.label: Insolvency practitioners
tabs.lead: Before closing the Notion, Jira or GitHub accounts, check whether their content can be given value.

steps.title: Case referral
steps.text: You tell us the company and which online tools are still active; we quickly assess the archive's potential.

steps.title: Protective export if needed
steps.text: If unpaid subscriptions put the accounts at risk, we can run a protective export before they are closed.

steps.title: Inventory under NDA
steps.text: Review of tools, volume and age of the content.

steps.title: Firm offer
steps.text: Offer in the usual format for asset sales, with no conditions precedent.
steps.detail: 10% deposit by bank cheque, bank certificate of funds, declaration of independence (art. L642-3 of the French Commercial Code).

steps.title: Authorization, deed and preparation
steps.text: Authorization by the supervising judge, signature of the deed, then export, preparation and deletion of raw exports.

aside.title: For the procedure
items: An additional source of proceeds, separate from the software, brand and domain names
Those assets stay in the estate and remain free to be sold
The export and preparation work set out in our offer is at our expense, as are deed costs

protection.label: Confidentiality
protection.title: Who will see what| of your company?
protection.intro: Prepared content is passed, under licence, to teams that train and evaluate AI models. Here is what they receive, and what they do not.

items.title: Your company name is removed
items.text: Your company name and brands are removed from the content: recipients do not know which company it comes from.

items.title: Authors are pseudonymized
items.text: Staff names, usernames and addresses are replaced with consistent pseudonyms, keeping who replied to whom without revealing who they are.

items.title: Customers and personal data removed
items.text: Customer names and personal data found in the text are removed.

items.title: Technical secrets removed
items.text: Keys, tokens and technical credentials are detected and removed.

items.title: What cannot be cleaned is left out
items.text: Content that cannot be sufficiently stripped of identifying elements is not passed on.

items.title: Raw exports deleted, access limited
items.text: Original exports are deleted after delivery. Only the people who need them have access, and every access is logged.

protection.restriction: Recipients receive a licence limited to training and evaluating models. They obtain no right to run, distribute or commercialize your software.

aiDevelopers.label: Buyers
aiDevelopers.title: For teams that train| and evaluate AI models
aiDevelopers.text: Real software development histories, with rights cleared by a written licence.
items: Linked sequences: ticket, specification, code change and review, in their real order
Executable environments where the history allows: the agent starts from the repository state before a change, receives the original request, and its proposal is checked against the project's tests
Traceable provenance: each dataset is tied to its licence, with the agreed scope and exclusions
Content prepared under one protocol: company not identified, authors pseudonymized, secrets and personal data removed

items.q: Do you take our source code?
items.a: It can be part of the scope, if you agree. The licence does not take away your ownership and only permits its use to train and evaluate AI models, with no right to run, distribute or commercialize the software.

items.q: What rights do we need to hold?
items.a: You must hold the rights to the licensed content. That is why code written for clients or under a third-party licence is excluded. This is checked during the inventory.
It depends on usable volume, technical depth, continuity of the history and the rights available. It is a fixed amount, written into the agreement and paid at signature.
Teams that train and evaluate AI models, under licence. They receive content from which your company name, authors' identities, personal data and technical secrets have been removed.
No. Slack, Teams and email are always excluded, as are HR and legal spaces, customer files and production databases.
No. You keep your content and can continue to use it as you wish.

value.label: Why this content has value
value.title: What has value| is the path from a problem to its resolution.
value.intro: On its own, an internal document is worth little. Linked together, your tools show how a team actually worked on real situations.

chain.title: The ticket
chain.text: describes a problem or a request, with its context.

chain.title: The specification
chain.text: sets out the intended solution and its constraints.

chain.title: The code
chain.text: shows the change that was actually made.

chain.title: The review
chain.text: shows the corrections, trade-offs and sign-off.

value.usage: These sequences are used to train and test AI models on software development tasks: understanding a request, finding the relevant context, proposing a change and checking the result. That is why the links between tickets, documents and code matter as much as the content itself.

economics.label: Payment
economics.title: How we assess| your content
economics.intro: There is no price list: each body of documentation is assessed case by case.

items.a: Real software projects, several years of history, and above all links between tools: tickets connected to specifications, code and reviews.
Usable volume, the technical depth of the exchanges, continuity of the history and the rights you hold over the content.
A fixed amount, written into the licence agreement and paid at signature.

items.q: If the archive is not a fit
items.a: We do not make an offer on every case. The assessment may conclude that a licence is not relevant; we will tell you plainly.
